azurerm_virtual_network_peering.peering declares depends_on = [module.networking], but module.networking is already an implicit dependency: the peering's virtual_network_name/resource_group_name/remote_virtual_network_id read local.combined_objects_networking, which is merge(module.networking, var.remote_objects.networking), so Terraform already orders the peerings after the virtual networks.

azurerm_virtual_hub_connection.vhub_connection declares depends_on = [module.networking], but the dependency is already inferred: remote_virtual_network_id resolves through local.combined_objects_networking, which merges module.networking, so Terraform already creates the vnets first.

azurerm_virtual_hub_connection.vhub_connection declares depends_on = [module.virtual_wans], but it already implicitly depends on module.virtual_wans:output.virtual_hubs via the virtual_hub_id attribute, which forces the virtual hubs (and their virtual WAN) to exist first.

data.external.ase_ilb_ip declares depends_on = [azurerm_template_deployment.ase], but the dependency is already implicit: the program argument interpolates azurerm_template_deployment.ase.outputs, which forces the ASE ARM deployment to complete before the external data source runs.

azurerm_private_dns_a_record.a_records declares depends_on = [azurerm_template_deployment.ase], but that ordering is already guaranteed transitively: the records attribute reads data.external.ase_ilb_ip.result, and the external data source both implicitly and explicitly depends on the ASE template deployment.

null_resource.grant_admin_consent declares depends_on = [azuread_service_principal.app], but the service principal is already an implicit dependency: the local-exec provisioner's environment block references azuread_service_principal.app.id and azuread_application.app, so Terraform already creates both before running the consent script.

azurerm_site_recovery_replication_policy.policy declares depends_on = [azurerm_recovery_services_vault.asr_rg_vault], but the policy already implicitly depends on the vault through its recovery_vault_name attribute, so the explicit depends_on adds nothing.
azurerm_vpn_gateway.s2s_gateway declares depends_on = [azurerm_virtual_hub.vwan_hub], but the gateway already implicitly depends on the hub via its virtual_hub_id attribute.
azurerm_express_route_gateway.er_gateway declares depends_on = [azurerm_virtual_hub.vwan_hub], but the gateway already implicitly depends on the hub via its virtual_hub_id attribute.
azurerm_point_to_site_vpn_gateway.p2s_gateway declares depends_on = [azurerm_virtual_hub.vwan_hub], but the gateway already implicitly depends on the hub via its virtual_hub_id attribute.

azurerm_point_to_site_vpn_gateway.p2s_gateway declares depends_on = [azurerm_vpn_server_configuration.p2s_configuration], but the gateway already implicitly depends on the configuration via its vpn_server_configuration_id attribute.

azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks uses role_based_access_control.azure_active_directory with managed = true, which requires the Microsoft.ContainerService AAD-V2 feature to be registered on the subscription. The module's null_resource.register_aks_msi_preview_feature performs that registration (including a wait loop that can take ~30 minutes), but nothing links the cluster to it: the null_resource has no dependencies and the cluster does not depend on it, so Terraform may create the managed-AAD cluster before the feature registration completes. Add depends_on = [null_resource.register_aks_msi_preview_feature] on azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks.
